modules.title: 你會游泳嗎？
modules.title_py: Nǐ huì yóu yǒng ma?

modules.scene: First week at university. The campus sports club is looking for new members. You and your classmates ask each other which sports you can do, then arrange to go jogging together.
can_do: Say which sports I can and can't do (我會…／我不會…)
Explain why you can't exercise today (我的腳很痛，不能…)
Arrange to do sport together: day, time, meeting place
modules.exam_link: Sports & hobbies are a FREQUENT topic in TOCFL Band A: 聽力 Part 1 (pictures of sports) and Part 2. The difference between 會 and 能 is often used as a distractor in 聽力 Part 4.

tasks.why: (1) a learned ability → 會. (2) a place to swim → 游泳池. (3) 踢足球. (4) the condition of a sore foot → 不能. (5) expecting to recover → 能. 籃球 doesn't fit any blank.

tasks.why: Text: 星期六去游泳. A and D reverse the meaning; B mixes up details (every day is 跑步, not 游泳).

grammar.explain: 會 = knowing how to do something because you have learned/practised it (languages, sports, instruments). The negative is 不會. To ask: 你會…嗎？ or 你會不會…？ A short answer is just 會。／不會。

grammar.explain: 們 marks the plural for PEOPLE: 同學們, 朋友們, 老師們 (and the pronouns 我們/你們/他們). It is not used for things, and not when there is already a number: 三個同學 (not 三個同學們).

grammar.explain: 也 always goes AFTER the subject and BEFORE the verb (never at the start or end of the sentence like English 'too'). Negative: 也不 (not … either).

grammar.explain: 沒(有) denies that something HAPPENED/was done (usually in the past): 我昨天沒上課. 不, on the other hand, denies habits, wishes or the future: 我不上課 (I don't/won't go to class). There is no 了 after 沒.

grammar.explain: 就 before a verb stresses immediacy or determination: 明年就來 (coming as soon as next year — sooner than you'd expect), 就去臺灣！ (right, Taiwan it is!).
